raw_segments.text: But he knew well who it was, and the Trojans were greatly angered.
Akamas then bestrode his brother's body and wounded Promachus the Boeotian with his
spear, for he was trying to drag his brother's body away.
Akamas vaunted loudly over him, saying, Argyve archers, braggarts that you are, toil and
suffering shall not be for us only, but some of you too shall fall here as well as ourselves.
See how Promachus now sleeps, vanquished by my spear.
Payment for my brother's blood has not been long delayed.
A man, therefore, may well be thankful if he leaves a kinsman in his house behind him
